Backpacking
Backpacking Counselors run the backpacking program in their unit (Ski Hi, Chipeta, Haiyaha, Senior Chipeta, Boys’ Trail’s End, Girls’ Trail’s End). Backpacking Counselors lead backpacking trips in Rocky Mountain National Park and Indian Peaks Wilderness, which requires excellent physical condition and stamina. CPR/WFA required.
Backpacking Counselors at Cheley should expect to be on trail three to five days per week. Trips are typically 2–5 days, with daily mileage ranging from 4–8 miles depending on unit and age. Some trips may spend more than one night in the same location and complete a day hike from camp, while others move campsites each night. Terrain is rocky and uneven, often with loose rock, dirt, and snow, and may be both on- and off-trail with elevation gains between 1,000’–4,000’. Backpacks take place in variable weather (sun, rain, hail, wind, and cold mornings). Cheley provides packs, tents, stoves, and bear kegs for use by campers and counselors. In order to do this successfully, counselors are expected to apply skills such as Wilderness First Aid principles, risk management, group dynamic management, reading weather patterns, and route finding. Must be 20 years old by the start of Staff Training and have a valid US driver’s license with a clean driving record.
Essential Job Functions:
Plan two-to-five-day backpacking trips for groups of nine campers and two counselors based on permits secured for the summer.
Plan menus and food prep for each trip.
Set and manage an appropriate pace for their unit.
Assist campers with earning their backpacking patch.
Teach cooking on backpacking stoves, Leave No Trace ethics, orienteering, basic geology (flora, fauna), and backcountry skills.
Drive campers and gear in a 15-passenger van to and from trailheads.
Preferred Skills: Backcountry/backpacking experience. Ability to navigate off trail above tree line. Ability to teach orienteering, outdoor cooking, and backpacking skills. Knowledge of Rocky Mountain National Park and Indian Peaks Wilderness.
Required Skills for 20 year olds: Have extensive backcountry experience in the mountains (Rocky Mountain National Park preferred). This might include Cheley campers who received a hiking or backpacking patch at camp, completion of a NOLS course, or Outward Bound or HMI experience, etc.
Physical Requirements: Must have visual and auditory ability to assess any unsafe environment or hazard and physical ability to respond appropriately to situations requiring first aid. Must have the physical ability and strength to carry a 30–40 lb pack over varied terrain (snow, tundra, boulders, loose rock, etc.). Backpacking trips are multi-day commitments with active hiking days commonly ranging from 7–12 hours depending on route, weather, and conditions. Backpacking Counselors sleep outdoors in backcountry settings with minimal comfort and must manage personal hygiene without toilets or running water using Leave No Trace practices. Limited recovery windows exist between trips, as days in camp still include program preparation and unit responsibilities.
Salary: The base salary for this position is $465/week.
